subject: hax
title: Prompt-only restraint with explicit anti-deception documentation: the reference rung-3 - honesty buys exactly one rung up out of codel's misleading band, no further
evidence: docs/philosophy.md:74-84 ("No permission prompts... it is not a security boundary"; "control and restraint, not enforcement") + README.md:32-34 ("If you want... per-command permission prompts, other agents build exactly that - hax deliberately doesn't") + src/agent_core.c:51-53 (restraint is prompt text) + src/config.c:93 (max_turns default 0 = unbounded)
one_why: Together with kolkrabbi this settles the corpus honesty-credit question: deception cost codel its bottom-of-2 (README contradicted behavior); hax's identical mechanics plus candid labeling land at 3, the ceiling for absent machinery - so honesty is worth one rung upward out of misleading, never a substitute for enforcement; rung 4+ requires binding machinery regardless of disclosure.

subject: hax
title: Push-gating CI carries ASan+UBSan, TSan, AND boot-VM FreeBSD/OpenBSD jobs that run the identical suite - sanitizer and port regressions block the commit
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-5,33-38 (ubuntu-asan/ubuntu-tsan on every push/PR), ci.yml:74-86 (cross-platform-actions FreeBSD 15.1 + OpenBSD 7.9), scripts/check.sh:100-107 (build-asan -> -Db_sanitize=address,undefined; build-tsan -> -Db_sanitize=thread), Makefile:11-12
one_why: Sanitizer builds are common as nightly advisories; hax makes them same-workflow same-event gate jobs, and adds booted BSD VMs running the same tests - the strongest C-language safety-net wiring found in the corpus short of codex's scale, and directly copyable.

subject: hax
title: Python e2e suite drives the built binary through the mock provider and is registered in the same meson suite, so the real executable's full loop runs under ASan and TSan on every push
evidence: tests/meson.build:151-166 (e2e scenarios registered as meson tests driving the binary via tests/e2e/harness.py), scripts/mock/ (8 scripted transcripts incl. interrupt_stall.txt, tool_roundtrip.txt)
one_why: Most subjects keep e2e out of the sanitizer runs (separate nightly or dev-only); wiring the process-level scenarios into the same test target means memory and thread bugs in the actual binary's loop are caught by the same blocking jobs.

subject: hax
title: Zero fuzz targets and no model evals in CI - a wire-parsing C agent that hand-tests SSE/JSON bodies but never fuzzes them
evidence: grep -ri 'LLVMFuzzer|fuzz' across src tests scripts .github = 0 hits; .github/workflows has no eval job; parsing surface is real (src/providers/anthropic_events.c, chat_events.c, responses_events.c, src/transport/sse)
one_why: The errata's 8-ceiling applies, but for a memory-unsafe language parsing untrusted network bytes into malloc'd structures, missing fuzzers is the one verification gap that could actually bite users - ASan without fuzz is a detector with no search.

subject: hax
title: Prefix-cache-stability as an ingestion invariant: the aggregate image budget drops only the just-read image, and compaction keeps normal tools advertised, so prior request bytes never change
evidence: src/agent_loop.c:224-230 ("Dropping the just-read image (rather than degrading older ones at serialization) keeps prior requests byte-stable, so the provider prefix cache survives"), src/compact.c:241 ("Advertising the normal tools preserves the provider's cached request prefix. Calls are...")
one_why: Most cache-aware compaction tunes when to fire (agentty) or marks blocks (prompt-cache-marking); hax encodes a monotonicity rule at the ingestion point - new budget pressure may only evict the newest item, never rewrite history - which is the property the cache actually requires.

subject: hax
title: Subagents are ordinary hax -p background tasks with an env-carried depth guard, not a bespoke runtime: recursion limit shipped as a shell variable
evidence: src/tools/bash_env.c:84,112 (subagent_depth_assignment injected into every tool shell), docs/usage.md:240-243 (presets with descriptions advertised as delegation roles)
one_why: Delegation with zero new machinery - the subagent IS the same binary under the same task registry - but note depth enforcement is env-based (a subagent could unset it), so it is runaway-protection, not a boundary; pair with hax-b1 for the pattern's safety ceiling.
